title: HTTP Caching: Speed Up Your Web Apps

scenes.line1: Why do some pages load instantly?
scenes.say: Ever notice some sites load in a flash? Let's see how HTTP caching makes that happen.

scenes.label: Cache
scenes.sub: Cache-Control, ETag, and Expires set caching rules.
scenes.say: Browsers and CDNs use headers like Cache-Control, ETag, and Expires to decide when to reuse a response.
Efficient caching means less work for your servers, faster load times for users, and better scaling as your app grows.

scenes.title: CDN Cache for 1 Hour
scenes.say: Here's a real-world example. Cache-Control with max age set to one hour, and an ETag for version tracking.

scenes.question: Does ETag alone cache a resource?
scenes.wrong: Yes, ETag stores the file in cache.
scenes.right: No, ETag just helps validate if the resource changed. Cache-Control actually sets caching.
scenes.say: Watch out: ETag doesn't cache by itself. It just checks if a file changed. Cache-Control is what lets browsers store responses.
